name: Dictatus papae
summary: Pope Gregory VII issues the Dictatus Papae ('Dictates of the Pope'), 27 papal propositions asserting absolute supremacy of the papacy over all secular rulers and ecclesiastical institutions. Key claims: the pope alone can convoke general councils; the pope alone can call himself 'universal'; the pope can depose emperors; papal legates outrank all bishops; the pope can absolve subjects from loyalty to wicked rulers. Gregory's program transforms the papacy from a spiritual authority into an aggressive political actor that directly confronts secular rulers.

_quarry.structural_significance: Launches the Investiture Controversy; defines the medieval papacy's claim to universal sovereignty; sets the terms of the Church-State conflict that defines the High Middle Ages
